sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Des Plaines
sections.html:
An owner in Des Plaines can hire a broker, go it alone, or take cash from a purchaser who buys the house as it is. Repair needs, tenants in the unit and a firm closing date tend to decide which path fits.

  • A full listing can fetch strong prices where the middle home value is $335,600, but it brings showings, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • Selling alone skips the commission and makes the contract and disclosures your job.
  • A cash deal shortens the calendar and suits estates, rentals and houses with postponed maintenance.

Because Des Plaines sits beside O'Hare and two tollways, buyers range from commuters to investors who want rentals near the airport and the Metra line.

Whichever you choose, ask each buyer or agent for a written net figure that subtracts the transfer taxes, recording fees, repairs and months of carrying costs. A higher headline price can leave you with less than a lower, faster offer.

Des Plaines is a Cook County city just north of O'Hare International Airport, with 58,772 residents, down 3.1 percent from 2020. Owners live in most homes.

Because 92.3 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, few houses change hands, which leaves sellers with fewer recent nearby sales as price guides. Ask an agent or cash buyer to show the sales they used.

Fewer sales also means a buyer paying cash may negotiate harder, because the comparison pool is thin. A written offer with a firm closing date gives you something concrete to weigh against a longer listing.

A buyer or lender will ask about flooding, and the Des Plaines River runs just east of downtown. Disclose any basement water or insurance claims and keep your repair receipts. The O'Hare station nearby averages 38.4 inches of snowfall, which is hard on roofs and gutters, so expect inspectors to look closely there.

One local quirk affects sellers: addresses inside city limits use the Des Plaines numbering system, while unincorporated parts of Maine Township with a Des Plaines mailing address follow Chicago's grid. Confirm with the city whether your parcel is incorporated, since that decides which city rules and which transfer tax apply.

Spring storms can turn severe here too, so inspectors and insurers may ask about roof age and past storm repairs. Keep records of any shingle, gutter or sump pump work you have done, and hand them to the buyer along with the disclosure report.

sections.h2: Cook County recording and transfer taxes
sections.html:
A Des Plaines deed is recorded by the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. A deed costs $107, a total that folds in the GIS, document storage and rental housing support fees, plus $5 per document for mail-back recording.

Three layers of transfer tax can apply, and the seller is the party liable on each:

  • State of Illinois: .50 per $500.00 of value, matching the rate in 35 ILCS 200/31-10.
  • Cook County: .25 per $500.00.
  • City of Des Plaines: 2.00 per $1,000.00, evidenced by a rubber stamp, with a $10.00 fee for exempt transfers.

Phone the city at 847-391-5325 to confirm the stamp before closing. Your contract can shift who pays, so ask the closing agent to show each line on the settlement statement.

The recording office accepts mail-back requests and the title company can usually submit the deed electronically, so you rarely need to travel downtown yourself. If the deed or declaration has an error, recording can be rejected and the closing delayed, which is why the title company reviews both before you sign.

Cook County splits the year's tax into two bills. The first equals 55 percent of last year's total and is typically due March 1, while homeowner and senior exemptions show up on the second. Interest on late payments runs 1.5 percent monthly.

Values come from the Cook County Assessor, and Maine Township, which covers parts of Des Plaines, is reassessed on a three-year cycle. Appeals go first to the Assessor and then to the Board of Review, each with its own window that moves by township every year. Check the Assessor's calendar for the next opening.

Have the PIN ready when you talk to the Treasurer or Assessor, because Cook County identifies every parcel by a 14-digit number. Your closing agent will explain how the year's bill is divided at the table.

If the second bill is unpaid when you sell, the balance comes out of your proceeds at closing. Ask the title company for the payoff figure before you set a closing date, and check that any homeowner or senior exemption was applied, since a missing exemption raises the bill you and the buyer are splitting.

sections.h2: Rentals and repair permits before a sale
sections.html:
Rental owners in Des Plaines need a rental license, and an ordinance passed on February 2, 2009 makes them complete Phase 1 of the Crime Free Multi-Housing Program. A first-time license applicant must attend the seminar beforehand.

Repair permits are filed online through the city's self-service portal, and express guides exist for sheds, decks, fences, driveways, roofs and non-structural kitchen or bath remodels. The 2021 I-Codes took effect January 1, 2026, and construction hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday. Inspections of rental dwellings or permitted work are booked at 847-391-5382 or permits@desplainesil.gov.

Closing out open permits before listing keeps unfinished work from surfacing late in a sale. Construction work in the city also needs a registered contractor, and registration runs through the same online portal, so confirm a contractor is registered before repairs start.

If you plan to sell a rental, the city's rental dwelling inspection line is a useful first call, since it lets you learn what an inspector would flag before a buyer's inspector does.

Once you accept an offer, the title company orders a search, prepares the deed and collects the transfer tax payments. You will sign the deed and a settlement statement, and the lender or lienholder is paid off from the proceeds. Cash buyers skip the appraisal and lender review, which is where most of the delay in a financed sale comes from.

Gather your PIN, your latest tax bill, any permit paperwork and, for a rental, the license and leases before you accept. If the sale involves a rental with tenants, ask the buyer in writing whether they will keep the tenants and how deposits will be credited.

faqs.q: Who is liable for transfer tax on a Des Plaines sale?
faqs.a: The seller is shown as liable for the state, county and city taxes. Your contract can allocate it differently, so confirm with your closing agent.

faqs.q: Where is a Des Plaines deed filed?
faqs.a: With the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. Title companies can also submit deeds electronically.

faqs.q: Is a license needed to lease my Des Plaines house?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental property owners must obtain a license and complete the Crime Free Multi-Housing seminar before a new license is issued.

faqs.q: Does a Des Plaines mailing address mean I am in the city?
faqs.a: Not always. Some unincorporated Maine Township addresses carry a Des Plaines mailing address but follow Chicago's numbering. Ask the city to confirm that your parcel is within the limits.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Des Plaines assessment?
faqs.a: Cook County sets new filing windows by township each year, first with the Assessor and then with the Board of Review. Check the Assessor's assessment calendar for the next opening.
